issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Partner-group activity events show the wrong relative time and sort out of order in the partner chat thread, because the /events endpoint serializes their UTC timestamp WITHOUT a Z suffix while every sibling timestamp in the same thread DOES append Z.

ROOT CAUSE (offset-less UTC — same class as the already-fixed social-feed + coach-social cases, but a distinct THIRD endpoint):
- Backend: app/routes/partner_groups.py:1250 (GET /partner-groups/<group_id>/events) returns 'created_at': r.created_at.isoformat() with NO Z. PartnerGroupEvent.created_at is a naive UTC column (db_models.py:2286, default=datetime.utcnow). The codebase convention is .isoformat() + "Z" (admin_v2/ai_dashboard.py, coach.py:85, and the partner-group MESSAGE serializer backend.py:5617/5679/5748 all append Z).
- Frontend: SessionStartedCard.tsx:29 and MealLoggedCard.tsx:28 compute relativeTime = Date.now() - new Date(iso).getTime(). An offset-less ISO string is parsed as LOCAL time, so for the primary market (IST, +5:30) a just-created event is read ~5.5h in the past. PartnerChatThread.tsx:292 also uses timestampOf(e.created_at) as the interleave sortKey, while chat messages use sent_at (which IS Z-suffixed / true UTC).

EXPECTED: an event that just happened shows "just now"; events and messages interleave in true chronological order.
ACTUAL (IST viewer): a just-happened "Mike started Push A" / meal-logged card shows "5h" ago; and because same-moment messages carry a Z (real UTC epoch) while events are shifted -5.5h, events sort ~5.5h earlier than messages that actually happened at the same time, so events cluster wrongly early in the thread. US/negative-offset viewers hit the mirror case: relativeTime clamps with Math.max(0,...) so everything reads "just now".

REPRO: open /partners/:groupId as an IST-timezone user; have a group member start a session or log a meal; observe the event card timestamp ("5h" instead of "just now") and its position relative to same-time chat messages.

FIX: append Z in partner_groups.py:1250 (r.created_at.isoformat() + "Z") to match the message serializers — one line, mirrors the b3f0/c1a7 fixes. (partner_groups.py:1393 reaction created_at is offset-less too but renders no relative time; optional for consistency.)
issues.author: shakeebshaan

fix.description: Root cause: the GET /partner-groups/<id>/events endpoint serialized each event's UTC created_at with .isoformat() but WITHOUT a 'Z' suffix, while every sibling timestamp in the thread (chat messages) does append Z. The app parsed the offset-less string as LOCAL time, so for IST users a just-created event card showed '5h' ago instead of 'just now' and sorted ~5.5h out of order against messages. Fix: append '+Z' to the events serializer (and the DM-reaction serializer) so both are true UTC, matching the message serializers. Capture shows the thread now rendering a just-logged meal as 'just now' and a 6-min-old session as '6m', in correct order.

judge.note: Root-caused + one-line fix mirroring the two prior offset-less-UTC fixes; backend regression test asserts Z-suffix (32/32 green); scenario capture confirms FE renders correct relative time + order; deployed live to prod.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Goal ETA on the Log-Weight "Goal Progress" card projects the goal date from an EWMA-SMOOTHED weekly rate but divides it into an UNSMOOTHED remaining distance, and reads trend direction from a single raw weigh-in — so the projected date is wrong by the daily water-weight swing on ~every view, and can invert outright.

ROOT CAUSE (src/pages/LogWeight.tsx:394-404 + src/lib/goal-eta.ts): computeGoalEta gets ratePerWeekKg = weightTrend.ratePerWeek (EWMA alpha=0.25, whose entire purpose is to cancel the 0.5-1.5 kg daily water/sodium noise), but remainingKg = goalProgress.remaining and direction = goalProgress.direction — both derived from goalProgress.currentKg = last_log.weight_kg, the RAW latest reading (seeded into the input at line 94, used at rest at lines 318/337/340-341). Smoothed rate + unsmoothed distance = apples-to-oranges.

MANIFESTATION 1 (distance error, ~every view): goal 75 kg, EWMA trend 76.2 kg descending -0.35 kg/wk -> true remaining 1.2 kg -> ~3 wk. If today's raw last_log came in at 77.5 kg (normal high-water morning) -> remaining = |77.5-75| = 2.5 -> weeks = round(2.5/0.35) = 7 -> "On track for <date> - ~7 wk". Projected date off by ~4 weeks from one noisy reading, and it jerks daily with water weight — defeating the EWMA the rate half already applies.

MANIFESTATION 2 (direction inversion): goal 75, EWMA trend 76.2 still descending -0.35 kg/wk, but the latest saved reading dipped to 74.0 kg (dehydrated morning; below goal though the trend is clearly above). goalProgress.direction = currentKg(74.0) < goalKg(75) -> "gain"; computeGoalEta towardGoal for "gain" needs rate>0 but rate is -0.35 -> off_track -> card shows "Not trending toward your goal yet - Keep logging to project your goal date." while the Goal Progress bar directly above reads ~99% and the trend caption shows the user steadily losing toward goal. Opposite of reality.

EXPECTED: the ETA remaining distance AND direction should be measured from the SAME EWMA-smoothed weight the rate comes from (weightTrend.kg) — remaining = |weightTrend.kg - goalKg|, direction from weightTrend.kg vs goalKg — so a single noisy weigh-in cannot swing or invert the projection.

REPRO: /log-weight with >=3 logged points and a live goal; have the most recent saved weigh-in deviate from the smoothed trend by ~1-2.5 kg (routine daily fluctuation). The "~N wk / On track for <date>" shifts by weeks vs the trend-implied ETA; when the raw reading crosses the goal line the card flips to "keep logging". tsc + the pure goal-eta.ts unit tests pass — the defect is the input wiring in LogWeight.tsx, not the helper.

FIX: pass remainingKg = |weightTrend.kg - goalKg| and derive direction from weightTrend.kg vs goalKg (the EWMA trend), instead of goalProgress (raw last_log / live input).
issues.author: shakeebshaan

fix.description: Root cause: LogWeight.tsx fed computeGoalEta a smoothed EWMA rate but an UNSMOOTHED remaining distance + direction (goalProgress.remaining/direction, both from the raw last_log weight) - so one noisy weigh-in swung the projected date by weeks and could invert direction to a false 'keep logging'. Fix: remaining = |weightTrend.kg - goalKg| and direction from weightTrend.kg vs goalKg (same EWMA weight the rate uses). Proof: raw last_log dipped to 74.0 kg below the 75 kg goal while EWMA trend ~76 kg descending - pre-fix inverted to 'keep logging'; post-fix reads 'On track for Jul 19, 2026'. tsc clean, goal-eta unit 8/8.

judge.note: Exact root-cause fix (matches the bug report's prescribed wiring change); surgical 12-line edit in LogWeight.tsx; full-screen 390x844 proof on the correct /log-weight screen shows the manifestation-2 inversion gone (raw 74.0 dip below goal now correctly reads 'On track for Jul 19, 2026' from the EWMA trend instead of 'keep logging'); tsc clean, goal-eta unit 8/8 green. Only caveat: proof uses a route.fulfill scenario mock since all onboarded accounts were deleted in the prelaunch cleanup - the mock faithfully drives the exact code path.

Confirmed slice-1 rescales MORE than 'targets only': preview builds macros_target directly from hp.target_kcal + UserProfile.target_{protein,carbs,fats}_grams (the exact columns PUT /profile/macro-targets writes), and _per_meal_targets() splits that daily target across each meal card (target_calories/protein/carbs/fat). So on save, BOTH the nutrition ring AND every per-meal card TARGET rescale on next fetch -- verified by construction. The ONE remaining piece of 'scaled accordingly' is re-cooking the actual assigned-meal PORTIONS (recipe ingredient grams) so a meal's real macros track its new per-meal target -- a deterministic slice (scale each meal's ingredient quantities by per_meal_target.kcal / current_meal_kcal, persist via UserMealModification). I did NOT ship it this headless tick because it mutates real plan data and I can't watch the rescaled portions render end-to-end: every onboarded/QA account was deleted in the prelaunch cleanup, so I have no live plan to verify against, and shipping an unverified DB mutation violates verify-before-ship + the board test gate. issues.reviewReason: On 'more than 10': root-caused the cap this tick. The screenshot shows 10, but the CURRENT shipped builder caps at 7 (BUILDER_MAX_DAYS, src/lib/onboarding-derive.ts:139) -- it was deliberately LOWERED 10->7 by QA i-20260710-7a3f, because the backend maps every training day to a distinct weekday (dow 1-7): plan_generator validates 1<=dow<=7, and workout_dow_to_python() resolves 'today's workout' as (day_index-1+offset) % 7. So day 8+ wraps onto day 1's weekday -- any cap above 7 silently collapses two training days onto one day (real data loss). That is why bumping the FE cap alone is NOT the fix and would regress 7a3f. The correct fix is the rotating microcycle I scoped earlier: store a cycle length N on the plan, resolve today's workout as days_since_start % N (decoupled from weekday), and update WorkoutSession creation + the weekly-review 'next week' logic. This same 'apply plan edits to next week without the weekday collapse' contract is ALSO the foundation slice for i-20260712-3d81 (add/remove exercise -> save-as-new-version -> propagate), so I'll build them on one shared backend contract. Blocker for verifying Day 11/12 resolve correctly at the 90 bar: all onboarded/QA accounts were deleted, so I can't drive a live multi-week plan headless. Unblock: restore/allow ONE onboarded test account and I'll land + verify the microcycle end-to-end.
